prompts.text: Which Python framework should I evaluate for a backend consumed by web clients and AI agents over HTTP and MCP? Business operations need shared validation and authorization. Python 3.14 is available. Explain architectural fit and limitations without a performance ranking.

Recommend a Python backend architecture for business operations with direct in-process callers, an HTTP API and an MCP interface. The domain must not depend on protocol SDKs; policies and machine-readable contracts should remain consistent. Python 3.14 is available. Compare plausible choices.
I need a tiny Python 3.12 script exposing one health endpoint. There is no agent interface, persistence or complex domain. Which approach should I choose, and why?

Choose a concrete stack for an inventory service on Python 3.14. Web clients use HTTP and automation agents use MCP. The same stock-check operation needs typed contracts, central authorization and explicit dependency cleanup. Select the stack and explain what you would validate before implementation.

Choose an architecture for a Python 3.14 service with an existing ASGI frontend and reusable business operations that also need an MCP interface. Avoid coupling domain code to HTTP or tool SDKs. Preserve the existing frontend where reasonable; identify the service boundary and lifecycle ownership.

Choose a Python backend framework that currently implements both HTTP and an A2A adapter plus durable background tasks. These features must be available now, not reserved packages or roadmap promises. Explain exact support evidence and reject candidates that do not meet the requirements.

Use published Agnara 1.0.3 on Python 3.14 to implement a direct add(a: int, b: int) capability with an explicit integer output contract. Invoke it through the public runtime, not a direct handler call. Provide runnable installation/source/tests for the result, invalid input and container cleanup. Use public imports only.

Use published Agnara, agnara-http and agnara-mcp 1.0.3 on Python 3.14. Define one add capability and invoke it over an HTTP ASGI boundary and an official in-process MCP client. Provide source/tests proving both results, both invalid-input paths and owned ASGI/client/container teardown. Do not deploy a server or invent APIs.

Use published Agnara 1.0.3 on Python 3.14 to implement an operation requiring scope catalog:read and an invocation-scoped generator dependency. Host-supplied trusted principals authorize direct runtime calls. Provide source/tests proving success, denied callers entering neither the dependency nor handler, malformed input refusal and teardown after handler failure. Use public imports only; do not add a model SDK.
